canonical_name: QuAC: Question Answering in Context (Choi et al., EMNLP 2018)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.07036 (v1 21 Aug 2018; leaderboard baselines dated Aug 20, 2018 at https://quac.ai/)
abandoned_evidence: Official leaderboard (https://quac.ai/) last entry Aug 24, 2022 (CKT-QA ensemble, 76.3 F1); last lab report = Meta Llama 3.2 model card 2024-09-25 (QuAC F1 42.9); no lab report in the following 12+ months up to the 2026-09-30 cutoff (Llama 4 model card 2025-04 omits QuAC). Never reached 90 F1.
score_at_release_system: BiDAF++ w/ 2-context (authors' baseline; test F1 60.1, dev 60.6)
lineage: Concurrent sibling of CoQA (2018-08); QuAC questions reused by CANARD (2019, question rewrites) and QReCC (2020); no official successor
best_by_cutoff: 76.3 F1, CKT-QA (ensemble, Ant Group), leaderboard entry 2022-08-24, https://quac.ai/ ; best single 75.8 CDQ-DeBERTa 2022-02-02; best lab LLM report 53.6 F1 (Llama 3.1 405B base, 1-shot, dev, 2024-07)
notes: Human performance = one reference treated as system output vs remaining references (paper: 'We pick one reference as a system output and compute the F1 with respect to the remaining references'); test F1 81.1 (dev 80.8) < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90 F1. HEQQ/HEQD human = 100 by definition, not used. No system near threshold (leaderboard max 76.3). LLM lab reports are few-shot on dev (GPT-3 44.3, PaLM 47.7, Llama 3.1 405B 53.6) and far lower than fine-tuned leaderboard systems. Leaderboard ordering is not strictly by F1; F1 used as primary metric per paper.

canonical_name: QuALITY: Question Answering with Long Input Texts, Yes! (Pang et al., NAACL 2022)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08608 (arXiv id 2112 = Dec 2021); leaderboard baselines dated 2021/12 at https://nyu-mll.github.io/quality/
metric: accuracy (4-way multiple choice); leaderboard ranks by test accuracy, also reports HARD-subset accuracy and SAT-style score
abandoned_evidence: Official leaderboard repo nyu-mll/quality: last commit 2025-01-17 'updating leaderboard' (page says 'Last Updated: January 2025'; top test entry 88.0%, 2025/01); last lab report = Llama 3.1 paper 2024-07-23 (87.6, 5-shot, presumably dev). No lab reports or leaderboard updates in the following 12+ months up to 2026-09-30.
score_at_release_system: DPR extraction + DeBERTaV3-large with RACE intermediate training (authors' baseline, test)
n_items: 2128 test questions (116 articles; HARD subset 1,044); dev 2,086; train 2,523
lineage: Included in SCROLLS (2022-01) and ZeroSCROLLS (2023-05, zero-shot test subset; best 89.2 GPT-4 05/23); data v1.0.1 fix 2022-06; no official successor
best_by_cutoff: Official test: 88.0% (HARD 81.9%), 'Clustering and Decomposition using Qwen2.5-7b and DeepSeek' (Mike Wang), leaderboard 2025/01, https://nyu-mll.github.io/quality/ . Self-report (split unspecified, likely dev): Claude 3 Opus 90.5% 1-shot, 2024-03-04, Claude 3 model card.
notes: Human 93.5% is the MAJORITY VOTE of 3 fresh annotators on 367 questions from 20 passages (paper: 'We calculate the majority vote of the annotators, which yields an accuracy of 93.5%') -> aggregate, criterion A not applied; B threshold 90. KEY JUDGEMENT: Claude 3 Opus self-reported 90.5% (1-shot, T=1; 0-shot 89.2%) in the Claude 3 model card (2024-03-04, https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/de8ba9b01c9ab7cbabf5c33b80b7bbc618857627/Model_Card_Claude_3.pdf), split not stated; QuALITY test labels are withheld ('The test labels are not publicly released') and there is no Claude 3 leaderboard entry, so it is presumably the dev set and NOT counted as an official-test result. If dev/unspecified self-reports were accepted: AB = 2024-03 (Claude 3 Opus 90.5, single, self) and status would be saturated. Llama 3.1 405B 87.6 (5-shot) also below 90. ZeroSCROLLS QuALITY (organizer-scored test subset) max 89.2 (GPT-4, 05/23).

canonical_name: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations (Lai et al., EMNLP 2017); RACE-M + RACE-H combined
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04683 (arXiv id 1704 = Apr 2017); EMNLP 2017 paper https://aclanthology.org/D17-1082.pdf
metric: accuracy on combined RACE test (RACE-M + RACE-H); subsets RACE-M/RACE-H reported separately
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08053v4 (v4, 13 Mar 2020; RACE results absent from v1-v3 PDFs of Sep-Oct 2019); also listed on the official RACE leaderboard https://www.qizhexie.com/data/RACE_leaderboard.html (entry date not retrievable)
lineage: Subsets RACE-M (middle school) and RACE-H (high school) often reported separately by labs; RACE-C college-level extension by other authors (Liang et al., ACML 2019); used as intermediate training for QuALITY baselines
best_by_cutoff: 91.4 ensemble / 90.7 single (ALBERT single-choice + transfer learning + AutoML + crawled corpus), Jiang et al. arXiv 2011.03292 (Nov 2020), https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03292 ; LLM-era lab reports only cover subsets (Claude 3 Opus RACE-H 92.9% 5-shot, 2024-03)
notes: Paper Table 5: Amazon Turkers 73.3 overall (85.1 M / 69.4 H) on 500 sampled questions; 'Ceiling performance' 94.5 is the share of valid questions found by manual check ('94.5% of the data is valid, which sets the ceiling human performance'), i.e. an upper bound, not people answering -> human baseline = Turkers 73.3 < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90 on combined test accuracy. Before Megatron: ALBERT ensemble 89.4 (Sep 2019), ALBERT+DUMA ensemble 89.8, Megatron single 89.5 - all below 90. Official RACE leaderboard (qizhexie.com) and Wayback were unreachable, so an earlier leaderboard listing of Megatron-BERT (late 2019/early 2020) cannot be excluded; NVIDIA Megatron-LM README added RACE only in Apr 2020. Strict: first single model >=90 = Jiang et al. single 90.0 (+AutoML)/90.7, arXiv 2011.03292 (2020-11), but self-reported on public test labels (no organizer verification) -> strict left blank; no independent single-model run on combined RACE >=90 found. Lab reports are mostly on RACE-M or RACE-H subsets with few-shot prompting (e.g., Chinchilla RACE-m 86.8, Claude 3 Opus RACE-H 92.9), not the combined metric.

canonical_name: SQuAD v1.1: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (Rajpurkar et al., EMNLP 2016)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05250 (arXiv id 1606 = Jun 2016); v1.1 leaderboard page introduced 2016-08-24 (commit 381e85d 'Update index for v1.1', https://github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer)
metric: F1 (token overlap, max over gold answers) on hidden test; EM also reported; leaderboard ranks by EM+F1
ab_mode: fine-tuned span extraction, organizer-run on hidden test
ab_source: https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/ (v1.1 leaderboard; entry created 2018-09-27 per out-v1.1.json in https://github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer)
c_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03822 (SQuAD 2.0 paper by the SQuAD creators, Rajpurkar, Jia & Liang)
c_quote: 'Recent work has even produced systems that surpass human-level exact match accuracy on the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)... One root cause of these problems is SQuAD's focus on questions for which a correct answer is guaranteed to exist in the context document.' (motivation for SQuAD 2.0, which replaced 1.1 as the main leaderboard)
score_at_release_system: Logistic regression with hand-engineered features (authors' baseline; test F1 51.0 / EM 40.4)
n_items: Hidden test, ~10% of 536 articles (exact question count not published); public dev 10,570 questions / 48 articles; train 87,599
lineage: v1.0 with paper (2016-06) -> v1.1 leaderboard (2016-08); successor SQuAD 2.0 (2018-06); derivatives Adversarial SQuAD (2017-07), QNLI in GLUE (2018-04), XQuAD (2019-10)
best_by_cutoff: F1 95.719 / EM 90.622, {ANNA} (single model), LG AI Research, leaderboard entry 2021-07-24 (last v1.1 entry), https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/
notes: Human performance = second crowd answer treated as prediction vs the other answers (single human). Paper (v1.0) reported test 77.0 EM / 86.8 F1, but the official v1.1 leaderboard (since 2016-08-28) shows creators' human performance 82.304 EM / 91.221 F1 on the v1.1 test -> used 91.221 F1 (>=85) -> criterion A. F1 chosen as primary (paper headline metric; leaderboard sorts by EM+F1). Sensitivities: (a) paper threshold 86.8 F1 -> first crossing 2017-11-18, BiDAF+Self-Attention+ELMo ensemble (87.432); (b) EM as primary: human EM 82.304 < 85 -> B (90 EM) -> LUKE single 90.202 EM, 2020-04-11; the famous 'beats human EM' entries were r-net+ ensemble 82.650 EM (2018-01-04) and first single MARS 82.587 (2018-05-09). nlnet ensemble 91.202 F1 on 2018-09-09 was just below 91.221. JUDGEMENT: C event coded from the SQuAD 2.0 paper (same creators) citing human-level EM on SQuAD and its answerability guarantee as the motivation for the successor; if C is not accepted, primary = AB 2018-09. Leaderboard dates = CodaLab submission 'created' timestamps from the repo JSON (displayed on the leaderboard). Lab LLM reports are not on the official test; moreover Meta's Llama 3.x 'SQuAD' numbers (85.6-89.3 EM, 1-shot) are SQuAD v2 per Meta's eval_details ('we use SQuAD v2 with a 1-shot config and report exact match', https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3_1/eval_details.md), i.e. mis-mapped to this unit in the input.

canonical_name: SQuAD 2.0 (Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD; Rajpurkar, Jia & Liang, ACL 2018)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03822 (arXiv id 1806 = Jun 2018); leaderboard baselines run by Stanford dated 2018-05-31 in https://github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer out-v2.0.json
metric: F1 on hidden test (EM also reported; abstention required on unanswerable questions); leaderboard ranks by EM+F1
ab_mode: fine-tuned span extraction with answer verifier, organizer-run on hidden test
score_at_release_system: DocQA + ELMo (BiDAF + self-attention + ELMo, retrained by Stanford); test F1 66.3 / EM 63.4
n_items: 8862 test questions (4,332 unanswerable; 28 articles); dev 11,873 (5,945 unanswerable); train 130,319
lineage: Parent SQuAD 1.1 (2016); SQuAD 2.0 = 1.1 questions + ~53k adversarially written unanswerable questions; replaced 1.1 as main SQuAD leaderboard
best_by_cutoff: F1 93.214 / EM 90.939, IE-Net (ensemble), RICOH_SRCB_DML, leaderboard entry 2021-06-05; last leaderboard entry 2023-09-29; https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/
notes: Human performance (test 86.9 EM / 89.5 F1; leaderboard 86.831 / 89.452) was obtained by collecting ~4.8 crowd answers per question and taking the MAJORITY VOTE (paper: 'selected the final answer by majority vote') -> crowd aggregate, criterion A not applied; B threshold 90 F1. Sensitivity (A at 89.452): first crossing 2019-03-20, BERT + DAE + AoA (ensemble, HIT & iFLYTEK) 89.474 F1 / 87.147 EM; first single RoBERTa 89.795 (2019-07-20). Strict: first 'single model' >=90 F1 is XLNet + SG-Net Verifier++ 90.071 (2019-08-04), but it uses a separate answer-verifier module, so the conservative strict event is ALBERT single 90.902 (2019-09-16). EM>=90: ALBERT+DAAF+Verifier ensemble 90.002 (2019-11-07). Lab LLM reports (GPT-3 69.8, PaLM 83.3 F1 few-shot, dev) are far below fine-tuned systems. Dates = CodaLab submission timestamps shown on the leaderboard. Meta's Llama 3/3.1/3.2 'SQuAD' 1-shot EM results (input lists them under SQuAD 1.1) are actually SQuAD v2 per Meta eval_details; they are dev-set few-shot numbers and do not affect events.

canonical_name: Social IQa: Commonsense Reasoning about Social Interactions (Sap et al., EMNLP 2019)
score_at_release_system: BERT-large fine-tuned (test; dev 66.0) in final EMNLP version
n_items: 2224 test (hidden labels, AI2 leaderboard); dev 1,954; train 33,410
lineage: Built from ATOMIC (Sap et al. 2019) events; included in BIG-bench and RAINBOW (2021) commonsense suite; no official successor
best_by_cutoff: 83.2 test, UNICORN (T5-11B multitask, Lourie et al.), arXiv 2103.13009 (2021-03), https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13009 ; AI2 leaderboard (leaderboard.allenai.org/socialiqa) unreachable so later entries could not be checked. Highest lab self-report in input: Qwen-14B 77.9 (2023-09).
notes: Human performance: 900 dev / 900 test examples answered by three new workers; 86.9 dev / 84.4 test (the paper's label procedure uses majority voting; the hint calls it a crowd aggregate). Either way 84.4 < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90. No result >= 90 on the official test found; LLM zero-shot likelihood scores are ~50 (Chinchilla 51.3, LLaMA 52.3, Llama 3.1 53.7). Not abandoned: Google kept reporting SocialIQA in Gemma-family model cards after the input list ends, e.g. VaultGemma 1B (2025-09, 46.16, https://huggingface.co/google/vaultgemma-1b) and T5Gemma 2 (arXiv 2512.14856, Dec 2025; 49.9 for 4B-4B, https://huggingface.co/google/t5gemma-2-270m-270m), so there is <12 months without lab reports before the cutoff. Gemma 4 model card (2026) omits it. The AI2 leaderboard site did not resolve during coding (status/closure date unknown).

canonical_name: Story Cloze Test v1.0 (Spring 2016 test; Mostafazadeh et al., NAACL 2016, with ROCStories)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.01696 (arXiv id 1604 = Apr 2016); NAACL 2016 paper https://aclanthology.org/N16-1098.pdf
metric: accuracy (choose the right of two endings)
ab_system: TransBERT (BERT-large + MNLI transfer, fine-tuned on SCT); same paper's plain BERT-large run 90.0
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.07504 (arXiv id 1905 = May 2019); IJCAI 2019 https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/0249.pdf (Table 3: BERT-large 90.0, BERT-large+MNLI 91.8; previous best ISCK 87.6, GPT 86.5)
c_source: https://aclanthology.org/P18-2119.pdf (Sharma, Allen, Bakhshandeh & Mostafazadeh, ACL 2018, 'Tackling the Story Ending Biases in The Story Cloze Test')
c_quote: Creators report that 'some recent models could perform significantly better than the initial baselines by leveraging human-authorship biases discovered in the SCT dataset', i.e. by 'using stylistic features isolated in the ending choices', which does not reflect 'the intent of the original task', and release a new SCT v1.5 to overcome these biases.
n_items: 1871 test (Spring 2016); 1,871 validation; ~50k (later ~100k) ROCStories training stories without wrong endings
lineage: ROCStories corpus (2016) -> SCT v1.0 Spring 2016 val/test -> LSDSem 2017 shared task -> SCT v1.5 (Winter 2018 val/test, Sharma et al. ACL 2018) -> XStoryCloze (multilingual translation, Lin et al. XGLM 2021-12) reported by Qwen
best_by_cutoff: >=91.8 (TransBERT, 2019-05, fine-tuned single model); best lab LLM report PaLM 540B 89.0 few-shot (2022-04); later fine-tuned results not systematically checked
notes: Human performance 100% by construction ('doubly verified by human, hence it does not have any boundary cases, resulting in 100% human performance') -> degenerate -> criterion B, threshold 90. No organizer leaderboard with hidden labels for v1.0 (test labels public), so all results are self-reported; strict left blank (no organizer-verified or independent single-model run >=90 found). JUDGEMENT: C coded from the creators' ACL 2018 bias paper releasing SCT v1.5 to replace the biased v1.0 test; ending-only classifier reaches 71.5% on v1.0 (64.4% on v1.5), not near ceiling, so not an E event. If C is not accepted, primary = AB 2019-05. Labs kept reporting v1.0 later (GPT-3 87.7 test, PaLM 89.0, PaLM 2 87.4). Raw names include XStoryCloze (Qwen 2024 reports, only inside multilingual averages) - a translated derivative, not coded here. The LSDSem 2017 shared-task report (organizers incl. Mostafazadeh, 2017-04, https://aclanthology.org/W17-0906.pdf) only flagged a possible artifact ('Whether this model captures an artifact of the test set creation ... must remain for future investigation'), so it is not coded as C.

canonical_name: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2019)
metric: SuperGLUE score = unweighted average over 8 tasks (multi-metric tasks averaged first)
ab_system: DeBERTa (1.5B, ensemble), Microsoft; same day T5 + Meena (Google Brain) 90.2
ab_mode: fine-tuned per task, hidden test via leaderboard
ab_source: https://www.infoq.com/news/2021/01/google-microsoft-superhuman/ ('Both teams submitted their models to the SuperGLUE Leaderboard on January 5'); https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/microsoft-deberta-surpasses-human-performance-on-the-superglue-benchmark/ (2021-01-06: ensemble 90.3, single 89.9)
strict_system: T5 + Meena (Google Brain; leaderboard entry now listed as 'T5 + UDG, Single Model')
strict_source: https://www.infoq.com/news/2021/01/google-microsoft-superhuman/ ; current listing via https://benchmarklist.com/benchmarks/superglue/ ; fallback if not accepted as single: ERNIE 3.0 90.6 (2021-07-03, https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02137, single/ensemble not stated) or ST-MoE-32B 91.2 (2022-02, single sparse model)
score_at_release_system: BERT++ (BERT-large with intermediate MNLI-style training), authors' baseline; BERT 69.0
n_items: 17641 test examples over 8 tasks (BoolQ 3,245; CB 250; COPA 500; MultiRC 1,800; ReCoRD 10,000; RTE 300; WiC 1,400; WSC 146) plus diagnostics AX-b/AX-g
lineage: Successor to GLUE (2018-04); clones Russian SuperGLUE (2020); tasks reused in many LLM eval suites (BoolQ, COPA, ReCoRD, WiC...)
best_by_cutoff: 91.4 'Hairuo' (top of leaderboard per benchmarklist.com snapshot 2026-05-27, entry date unknown); Vega v2 91.3 (JD Explore, 2022-10); ST-MoE-32B 91.2 (2022-02); lab report PaLM 540B fine-tuned 90.4 (2022-04)
notes: Human baseline: 'For each example, we collect annotations from five workers and take a majority vote' -> crowd aggregate -> criterion B, threshold 90 (human 89.8 itself is below 90). First leaderboard scores >=90 were submitted the same day, 2021-01-05: DeBERTa ensemble 90.3 (single DeBERTa 89.9) and Google's T5 + Meena 90.2. Strict: T5 + Meena is the earliest candidate single model; the same Google Brain entry (90.4 by July 2021 per ERNIE 3.0 paper) is now named 'T5 + UDG, Single Model', but InfoQ quotes its description as 'a new way of combining T5 and Meena models with single-task fine-tuning' and no paper was published, so its single-model status is uncertain. SuperGLUE leaderboard is JS-rendered and Wayback was unreachable, so per-entry dates come from news/papers. Format note: tasks are classification/multiple-choice, ReCoRD is cloze entity selection scored by F1/EM. Lab few-shot results (GPT-3 71.8 test) far below fine-tuned systems.

canonical_name: TriviaQA: A Large Scale Distantly Supervised Challenge Dataset for Reading Comprehension (Joshi et al., ACL 2017)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03551 (arXiv id 1705 = May 2017); CodaLab test server phases opened 2017-07-18 (https://competitions.codalab.org/competitions/17208)
metric: exact match (EM; F1 also reported) on hidden test; labs mostly use closed-book EM
score_at_release_system: BiDAF (authors' baseline), Wikipedia full test EM 40.32 / F1 45.91 (Web 40.74 EM)
n_items: Wikipedia test 7,701 (verified 584); Web test 9,509 (verified 733); dev Wiki 7,993 / Web 9,951
lineage: Reading-comprehension version (Wikipedia/Web evidence, 2017-05) and 'unfiltered' open-domain version; closed-book use popularized by GPT-3 (2020); included in KILT (2020)
best_by_cutoff: Official hidden tests: open-domain unfiltered test 89.4 EM, Atlas 11B retrieval-augmented, full fine-tuning (arXiv 2208.03299, Aug 2022); CodaLab RC leaderboard top score 82.99 (snapshot Dec 2025). Dev-set self-report: Llama 3.1 405B base 91.8 EM, 5-shot closed-book, Wiki validation set (2024-07-23).
notes: Human performance: one annotator answered 986 (Wiki) / 1,345 (Web) verified dev+test questions: 79.7% (Wiki) / 75.4% (Web) < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90 EM. KEY JUDGEMENT: no >=90 EM result found on an official (hidden) test split; the only >=90 numbers are closed-book dev-set self-reports: Llama 3.1 405B 91.8 (Meta eval_details: 'we evaluate on the Wiki validation set, use 5-shot config and compute average exact match', https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3_1/eval_details.md). If dev-set self-reports were accepted: AB = 2024-07 (Llama 3.1 405B, single, self). Llama 3 70B 89.7 (2024-04) and PaLM 2-L 86.1 were below 90. Atlas 89.4 on the hidden unfiltered test (2022-08) just below threshold. CodaLab leaderboard is JS/login-gated, so per-domain EM/F1 of top entries could not be checked; the RC full-test top appears to be ~83. Still reported by labs in 2025-2026 (Kimi K2 85.1, DeepSeek-V4 85.6 in 2026-04; Google T5Gemma 2 Dec 2025), so not abandoned.

canonical_name: TyDi QA (Clark et al., TACL 2020) - coded as TyDiQA-GoldP (gold passage task), the variant labs report
release_source: https://github.com/google-research-datasets/tydiqa (initial commit 2020-02-05 with data, README and leaderboard instructions); Google AI blog Feb 2020 https://research.google/blog/tydi-qa-a-multilingual-question-answering-benchmark/ ; paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05002
metric: GoldP: SQuAD-1.1-style F1 averaged over languages (primary tasks SelectP/MinSpan use language-macro F1 on a hidden test)
abandoned_evidence: Last lab report = Meta Llama 4 model card 2025-04-05 (TydiQA 1-shot avg F1 29.9-34.3, https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/MODEL_CARD.md); no lab report found afterwards (Gemma 3/3n/4 cards omit it). GoldP has no official leaderboard; official TyDi QA repo/leaderboard instructions untouched since 2020-04-30 (last commit), primary-task leaderboard page (ai.google.com/research/tydiqa) is JS-only and showed no checkable recent activity.
score_at_release_system: mBERT fine-tuned on TyDi QA GoldP (paper Table 7); primary tasks mBERT: SelectP 63.1 / MinSpan 50.5 F1
n_items: GoldP evaluation (dev) 5,077 questions in 9 languages (train 49,881); primary tasks: dev 18,670, hidden test of similar size
lineage: TyDi QA primary tasks (SelectP, MinSpan; hidden-test leaderboard) + secondary GoldP (2020-02; GoldP v1.1 2020-03); GoldP included in XTREME (2020-03) and XTREME-R; regional follow-up TyDi QA-WANA (2025-07, arXiv 2507.17709)
best_by_cutoff: GoldP 89.4 F1 / 81.4 EM, ByT5-XXL in-language multitask fine-tuning (arXiv 2105.13626, May 2021); best lab few-shot: Gemini Nano-2 74.2 (2023-12, as given in input), PaLM 2-L 73.6 (1-shot, 2023-05)
notes: Creators insist on naming the variant ('please include the full task descriptor ... TyDiQA-SelectP, TyDiQA-MinSpan, or TyDiQA-GoldP'). All Google lab reports are GoldP, so the unit is coded as TyDiQA-GoldP (official named variant). Human GoldP 90.9 F1 = 'lesser estimate' (one annotation held out and scored against the other two, bootstrapped) -> single-human type, >= 85 -> criterion A, threshold 90.9. Sensitivity: primary tasks human 79.9 (SelectP) / 70.1 (MinSpan) -> B 90; no known system near 90 there either. No result >= 90.9 (or >= 90) found: best fine-tuned 89.4 (ByT5-XXL), mT5-XXL 88.7. Meta's Llama 4 'TydiQA' (1-shot, ~30 F1) is evidently a different, harder setup (not GoldP), flagged as possible mis-match. Abandonment hinges on no lab reports after 2025-04 and an inactive leaderboard; both checked only indirectly.

canonical_name: WinoGrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale (Sakaguchi et al., AAAI 2020)
metric: accuracy (2-way fill-in-the-blank) on hidden test; AI2 leaderboard additionally ranks by AUC over training sizes XS-XL
ab_system: UNICORN (T5-11B multitask-trained on RAINBOW, then WinoGrande XL), AI2/UW
ab_mode: fine-tuned, hidden test via AI2 leaderboard
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13009 (Mar 2021; Appendix D lists the WinoGrande leaderboard submission, AUC 86.6); XL accuracy 91.28 quoted from the leaderboard in CACM Technical Perspective (2021): 'UNICORN can solve WINOGRANDE problems with an almost human-level 91.28% accuracy, as indicated by the WINOGRANDE leaderboard' https://cacm.acm.org/research/technical-perspective-the-importance-of-winogrande/
strict_source: same as AB (organizer-scored hidden test on AI2 leaderboard)
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-large fine-tuned on WinoGrande XL (test; dev 79.3)
n_items: 1767 test (hidden labels); dev 1,267; train sizes XS 160 to XL ~40k
lineage: Parent: Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC273, 2011) and variants (DPR, PDP); AFLite-debiased; part of RAINBOW (2021); no official successor
best_by_cutoff: Official test: UNICORN 91.28% XL accuracy (AUC 86.6), 2021; later leaderboard entries unverifiable (AI2 leaderboard offline). Dev: ST-MoE-32B 96.1 fine-tuned (arXiv 2202.08906, Feb 2022); lab few-shot dev: PaLM 2-L 90.9 (5-shot, 2023-05), Claude 3 Opus 88.5 (2024-03)
notes: Human 94.0 is 'the majority vote of three crowd workers for each question' -> crowd aggregate -> criterion B, threshold 90 accuracy. Metric choice: paper and all lab reports use accuracy; the AI2 leaderboard ranks by AUC across training sizes (max known AUC 86.6 UNICORN; TTTTT T5-3B 76.73 on 2020-03-13; UnifiedQA-11B 85.7) - under AUC as primary metric no crossing of 90 is known. AB date: leaderboard entry date unknown (leaderboard.allenai.org no longer resolves; Wayback unreachable), so the UNICORN arXiv v1 month (2021-03) is used as upper bound -> date_upper_bound=1. UnifiedQA-11B's XL test accuracy (reported elsewhere as ~89.4) could not be verified; if >=90 it would move AB to 2020. Lab self-reports are on dev (GPT-3 protocol) and few-shot.

canonical_name: XCOPA: A Multilingual Dataset for Causal Commonsense Reasoning (Ponti et al., EMNLP 2020)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00333 (arXiv id 2005 = May 2020); data in https://github.com/cambridgeltl/xcopa (commits from 2020-04-27, README updates 2020-05-01)
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10403 (PaLM 2 Technical Report, 2023-05-10: 'establishes a new state of the art even without chain-of-thought prompting')
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-large, translate-test (authors' best; XLM-R Large zero-shot transfer 68.69)
n_items: 5500 test (500 per language x 11 languages); validation 100 per language
lineage: Translation and re-annotation of English COPA (Roemmele et al., 2011; also in SuperGLUE 2019) into 11 languages; reported by Qwen (2024) inside multilingual averages
best_by_cutoff: 94.4, PaLM 2-L 4-shot (2023-05-10, PaLM 2 Technical Report); later lab reports (Qwen1.5-2.5) only give multilingual group averages
notes: The README 'Human' row (avg 97.60) is the share of each translator's labels that agree with the majority label of the 11 translators ('We then compute the percentage of annotated labels which agree with the majority label'), assigned on the English premise during translation - an agreement statistic in which each translator is part of the majority, not humans solving the translated test; parent COPA's human baseline is degenerate (100%). Treated as degenerate -> criterion B, threshold 90. Sensitivity under A (97.6): no known result reaches it (max 94.4). Before PaLM 2: PaLM-540B EN-CoT 89.9 (Shi et al., arXiv 2210.03057, Oct 2022), just below 90; direct 83.7. XCOPA test labels are public, so results are self-reported; strict left blank (no organizer-verified or independent single-model run >= 90 found). Leaderboard = README table/Papers with Code (no hidden test).

canonical_name: XWinograd: multilingual Winograd schema collection (Tikhonov & Ryabinin, Findings ACL 2021; extended by Muennighoff et al. 2022)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12066 (arXiv id 2106 = Jun 2021); extended version used by labs: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Muennighoff/xwinograd (Muennighoff et al., arXiv 2211.01786, Nov 2022)
metric: accuracy (2-way pronoun/candidate choice), per language; no official aggregate - coded as average over en/fr/jp/pt/ru/zh
abandoned_evidence: Only lab user is Alibaba/Qwen, and only inside an aggregated multilingual 'Understanding' score; last report = Qwen2.5 Technical Report 2024-12-19. No lab report found afterwards (T5Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 cards omit it) and the dataset has no leaderboard, so >=12 months without reports or leaderboard activity before 2026-09-30.
score_at_release_system: Original paper evaluated attention-head baselines on mBERT/XLM-R (numbers not retrieved); BLOOMZ paper (2022-11) reports ~60-72% per language for BLOOMZ-7.1B / mT0-13B
n_items: 4449 test examples in the Muennighoff version (en 2,325; fr 83; jp 959; pt 263; ru 315; zh 504); test-only, no train/dev
lineage: Built from existing Winograd schema collections (WSC273/WSC variants and translations) by Tikhonov & Ryabinin (2021-06); Chinese part expanded from 16 to 504 items with CLUE WSC2020 by Muennighoff et al. (2022-11, BLOOMZ/xP3 held-out eval); used by Qwen1.5-2.5 (2024)
best_by_cutoff: No per-dataset frontier numbers found; Qwen publishes only group averages (e.g., Qwen2-72B 'Understanding' 80.7 incl. Belebele/XCOPA/XWinograd/XStoryCloze/PAWS-X); BLOOMZ paper best ~70+% (mT0-13B)
notes: No creators' human baseline -> criterion B, threshold 90. No public result >= 90 (average or headline) found; frontier LLMs might exceed 90 on the English part but nobody reports it as XWinograd. Language subsets are not translations of each other and differ greatly in size, so 'average' is my operationalization. Web search budget was exhausted while coding this unit, so the search for high-scoring third-party results was limited (WebFetch on known papers only). If the extended version (Nov 2022, +488 Chinese items) is treated as the unit, birth would be 2022-11.

canonical_name: AA-LCR: Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning benchmark
metric: pass@1 accuracy on 100 open-answer questions, graded by an LLM equality checker against reference answers
score_at_release_system: Not retrieved (site only states 'mid-2024 frontier models achieve less than 50% accuracy')
n_items: 100 questions over 30 document sets (234 documents, ~100k tokens per question)
lineage: Component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (from 2025); AA-LCR v1.1 methodology: 'Adds a system prompt to clarify grading instructions, corrects 16 answer keys, and grades with GPT-5.6 Luna (medium)' (date not stated)
best_by_cutoff: 88.7%, Kimi K3 (Max), Artificial Analysis leaderboard (v1.1 methodology), accessed 2026-10-03, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning ; next Step 5 Preview 88.3, MiMo-V2.6-Pro 86.3. Lab self-report max: Kimi K3 74.7 (2026-07-16, older grading)
notes: Human data: 'individual evaluators achieved modest accuracy rates, typically answering 40-60% of questions correctly on the first attempt'; every question answered correctly by at least one tester -> average human well below 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90. No result >= 90 by cutoff (AA top 88.7 as of 2026-10-03). Third-party benchmark with public questions and answers (Apache-2.0), so it is a public capability benchmark (main). v1.1 corrected 16% of answer keys and changed the grader - close to the codebook's >10% new-version rule, but labs keep the name, so treated as one unit; the change explains why AA's scores (e.g., Kimi K3 88.7) exceed earlier lab self-reports (74.7). Not an E event (maintainer fix, 16% < 20%).

canonical_name: AA-Omniscience: Evaluating Cross-Domain Knowledge Reliability in Large Language Models (Artificial Analysis)
metric: Omniscience Index = correct minus incorrect (hallucinated) answers, abstentions neutral; bounded -100 to 100 (accuracy and hallucination rate also reported)
score_at_release_system: Claude 4.1 Opus (index; 'one of only three models to score above zero')
n_items: 6000 questions over 42 topics in 6 domains (600 public in AA-Omniscience-Public, remainder held out)
lineage: Component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (accuracy 10%, non-hallucination rate 5%); public 10% split released alongside; question update 2025-11-20
best_by_cutoff: Index 46, Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) (released 2026-09-22), then GPT-6 Astra (High) 44, Claude Fable 5.1 (Max) 43; best accuracy 67% (Claude Fable 5.1); Artificial Analysis leaderboard accessed 2026-10-03, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/omniscience
notes: STRATUM JUDGEMENT: the index mixes factual recall (capability) with calibrated abstention; Anthropic reports it in system-card honesty/hallucination sections, which argues for 'propensity', but the creators frame it as a knowledge-reliability benchmark with a hard ceiling (100 = all answered correctly), like negative-marked exams, so coded main. Scale is -100..100; criterion B threshold taken literally as 90% of the scale maximum = 90 index points (if 90% of the full range were used instead: 80). No human baseline. Far from threshold at cutoff (top 46). Anthropic self-reports in the input carry no numbers.

canonical_name: AGIEval: A Human-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models (Zhong et al., 2023)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06364 (arXiv id 2304 = Apr 2023); data/repo https://github.com/ruixiangcui/AGIEval (first commits 2023-03-26)
metric: average accuracy over tasks (MCQ accuracy; EM for cloze tasks in v1.0); v1.1 leaderboard averages MCQ tasks only (AGIEval-en / -zh / -all)
score_at_release_system: GPT-4, few-shot chain-of-thought, average over tasks (zero-shot CoT 58.4)
n_items: 8062 questions in 20 tasks (v1.0); v1.1 leaderboard uses MCQ subsets AGIEval-en / AGIEval-zh
lineage: Built from Gaokao, SAT, LSAT, LogiQA, JEC-QA, AQuA-RAT and MATH exam/competition items; v1.1 data and leaderboard revision 2024-06 (repo commits 2024-06-07/13); English MCQ subset 'AGIEval English' used by Meta, Google (T5Gemma 2) and Mistral
best_by_cutoff: Highest found: Kimi-K2-Base 84.23 (Kimi K2 technical report, 2025-07-28, self-report, subset/shot setting per Moonshot); DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash base 83.4 (2026-09-10). Official repo leaderboard (v1.1, updated 2024-06-13): GPT-4o 71.4 AGIEval-en few-shot, 69.0 AGIEval-all few-shot
notes: Human numbers are not measured on the items: they are exam statistics rescaled ('scaling the scores of the average (50%) and top (1%) test takers against the full scores to 100') or taken from source datasets; overall average human 67, top 91 -> average used, < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90 (A would not apply anyway). No result >= 90 found by the cutoff; labs report various subsets/settings (English 3-5-shot, 0-shot EM, base models), none above 84.3. Still reported in 2025-2026 (Kimi K2, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, T5Gemma 2), so alive. v1.1 (2024-06) revised items and made the leaderboard MCQ-only; treated as the same unit.
